Query a store's datasets in DuckDB

Source: R/duckdb.R
store_duckdb.Rd

Creates one DuckDB view per dataset of the store's primary catalog (rasters excluded, the H3 index tables of geospatial datasets included), so that the datasets can be queried with SQL or with dbplyr. A view stores no data: DuckDB reads the Parquet files when a query runs, and only the columns and row groups the query needs. The file list comes from the catalog held by the connection st, so the views show the versions it knows: after store_refresh() call store_duckdb() again. One message names the views made.

Usage

store_duckdb(
  st,
  path = NULL,
  datasets = NULL,
  mode = c("native", "arrow"),
  spatial = FALSE,
  con = NULL
)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect(). It may be left out only with path, to reopen a file prepared earlier.

path

NULL for an in-memory database, or the path of a DuckDB database file (see "Database files").

datasets

NULL for every dataset, or full or short dataset names; their index tables are added.

mode

"native" or "arrow", see above.

spatial

TRUE loads the DuckDB spatial extension (downloaded on first use).

con

NULL to create a new connection, or an existing DuckDB connection made with bigint = "integer64" (H3 cells do not fit a double); path must then be NULL.

Value

The DuckDB connection, invisibly. Close it with DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE).

Details

The views are queried with SQL (DBI::dbGetQuery()), with dbplyr (dplyr::tbl(con, DBI::Id(schema = , table = )), or store_open(st, dataset, engine = "duckdb", con = con), whose collect() restores the R types and the geometry and which takes store_intersects()), and can be joined with your own tables. A lazy table on the connection can be written back to the store with store_write(). vignette("duckdb") shows each step.

  • View names: the first part of the dataset name is the schema, the other parts joined with __ are the view; a one-part name goes to schema main. "sales/daily" is the view sales.daily, "a/b/c" is a.b__c. Two datasets with the same view name, a first part rcs, or a first part equal to the name of an attached database (such as memory or system) abort.

  • mode = "native" (the default): DuckDB reads the files itself with read_parquet(), from the location a read would use. For locations on Google Cloud Storage a temporary DuckDB secret is created from the location's credential (see rcs_auth_gcs()); it lives only in this connection and holds an access token, valid for about an hour. After an hour of DuckDB work on a bucket, call store_duckdb() again: every call renews the secrets. The geometry column of geospatial datasets is of DuckDB type GEOMETRY, readable without the spatial extension.

  • mode = "arrow": the Arrow dataset the package opens for reads is registered in DuckDB and the view selects from it, so DuckDB needs no credential of its own; filters are pushed into the Arrow scan. The geometry column is WKB (BLOB). The registration lasts only as long as the connection: in a database file such views stop working once it is closed (see "Database files").

  • spatial = TRUE installs and loads DuckDB's spatial extension and, in arrow mode, adds a column geom (GEOMETRY) to geospatial views.

  • H3 cells are BIGINT columns, read into R as bit64::integer64; the macro rcs_h3_hex(x) turns them into hex strings in SQL.

The connection records its views in the table rcs.views (view, dataset, version, location, mode, refreshed in UTC) and the store's locations in rcs.store (role, uri); neither holds a credential. A connection serves one store. With datasets = NULL both tables are rewritten and the views of datasets no longer in the catalog are dropped; with datasets given only those views and rows are replaced. store_tables() lists what a connection holds.

Database files

With path, the views, the rcs tables and the tables you create live in a DuckDB file, created when missing. A file work.duckdb is attached as the database work, so no dataset may have the first part work. The file must lie outside every local location of the store, which a sync would carry it to.

Calling store_duckdb(st, path) again on the same file refreshes it: views are replaced to show the versions in st's catalog, views of deleted datasets are dropped, secrets are recreated, and your own tables and views are left untouched (a table or a view not made by store_duckdb() with a view's name aborts). store_duckdb(path = ) without st reconnects to the store recorded in rcs.store, with default credentials, and refreshes the same way.

A plain DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(dbdir = path), bigint = "integer64") also opens the file: your tables work, and native views work while their files exist, but they show the versions of the last refresh (a later write may have deleted those files, unless the store keeps history), views on Google Cloud Storage need a secret first, and views in arrow mode do not work until store_duckdb() is called again. store_tables() with st says which views are not current.

See also

store_tables(), store_open(), store_intersects(), store_write().

Examples

root <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-duckdb")
st <- store_connect(root, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(100, seed = 1), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 100 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-duckdb  2/2
#>   files sent  23.8 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
con <- store_duckdb(st)
#> ✔ DuckDB view (native mode, nothing read yet): `sales.daily`.
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT year, sum(qty) AS qty FROM sales.daily GROUP BY year")
#>   year  qty
#> 1 2023 1328
#> 2 2024 1028
store_tables(con, st)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   schema name  type  dataset     version          current
#> * <chr>  <chr> <chr> <chr>       <chr>            <lgl>  
#> 1 sales  daily view  sales/daily 0f9e01793cbea58a TRUE   
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
